steps.text: ...Lieutenant...
Lieutenant... Shearer... wake... up...
He sees a pair of hands reach out towards him.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: ...Lady Delphine?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Don't move. I'll carry you. We need to get back to the forward position that we captured.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We have to move before more Sarkaz arrive and fill this place with witchcraft bombs.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I—thank you—saving my life—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: No need. It was a brave soldier and nurse, Sarah, who saved your life.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: She used her Arts to protect you and the other wounded soldiers from the witchcraft bomb, despite her limited experience.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: It was her... wait, did she—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Don't worry, she just passed out. We've taken her to the forward position at the access port.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But you've all been exposed to high-Originium environments for too long...

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I knew the risks.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: You succeeded in reaching the access port?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I saw fire on the wall... it's out.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Is the battle for the walls over?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: No, it has only just begun.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Nachzehrer is locked in a standoff with the ducal alliance, relying on the city's defensive artillery and the elite troops.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Is there anything we can do?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Break through the access port, create a gap in the wall, and reveal a weakness in the Sarkaz lines.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Just like the alliance helped us... even if they didn't mean to.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Understood—*cough*—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Lieutenant Shearer, you are dismissed from this operation. That is an order.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Does that come from Siege—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: It comes from me.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Stand by at the forward position. You need to rest.

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: ♪Then may we call and savely syng,

steps.name: Excitable Soldier
steps.text: May the vast lands they keep owre kynge. ♪

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: ......His people, and alle his well-wyllynge. ♪

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: And give them grace wythoute endyng. ♪

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: Why aren't you singing?

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: Cheer up, man! I know, we're all hurt, but we're almost home!

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: ♪Then may we call and savely syng,

steps.name: Excitable Soldier
steps.text: ♪Victoria, yeve thankes for owre hom!

steps.name: Depressed Soldier
steps.text: V—Victoria, yeve thankes for owre hom! ♪

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: Here, you can have the rest of this ration. Couldn't finish it.

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: It's our first breakfast since we came back home. Got to fill up!

steps.name: Excitable Soldier
steps.text: Once the rest of our men make it into the city, we'll show those devils who really runs Londinium!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I don't like that song...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: What about you, Vina?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Don't ask her. She hums it in her sleep.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Hannah!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Shut your gob and eat up, Indra.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Or I'll take it, if you don't want it, and I'll lead the assault since you got hurt attacking the Confessarius passage.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Not a chance. It's just a scratch.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: A little scratch won't dull my fists. You're not gettin' ahead of me this time, Dagda.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I'll do another round of patrol and scout ahead once I'm done, make sure there's no mistake.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Military Commission set up defenses at this backup access port, which should only have been known to the workers who built the wall. This means they know the city much better than we expected.
I'm back from patrol, Lady Delphine.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Spare a ration? I haven't had breakfast yet.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Lieutenant?! I thought you were recovering from your injuries.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I'm a medic. I know how to restore a soldier to combat effectiveness as quickly as possible.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I understand my own body, Lady Delphine. I am ready to return to duty.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Giving your protective equipment to the wounded, getting exposed to high-Originium environments, and being in close proximity to a witchcraft bomb explosion... you know exactly what all this means, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: I do. A blood test is not possible now, but I understand the pathological progress of infection.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: What about it? Is that not normal in this place?
He looks around. Exemplars are crowded around the narrow passage.
The dust and Originium particles that cover their faces have not diminished the fire in their eyes at all.
They know what they are doing. They know the price they will pay.
But they are singing.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Delphine, do you give the Lieutenant permission to return to duty?
Delphine can see the painkiller injector that Shearer is trying to hide behind his back.
Without sufficient access to Oripathy suppressants, painkillers are the next best thing to deal with the suffering brought on by Oripathy.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Will you pull through?

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Of course, Lady Delphine. Never forget, I still have to see you go home and take back what is yours.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: ...You didn't need to do this.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: Neither did you.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: You want to witness what this ragtag team can achieve, what will come of this city. So do I.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Very well, Lieutenant. Back to your post.

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: What will Londinium be, once we drive out the devils, Vina?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Better than before, at least.

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: You know what I'd like to see? More flower shops, making the flowers cheaper, making it easier for me to find a girl to marry. Maybe a wealthy young woman. Or a widow who lost her husband.

steps.name: Excitable Soldier
steps.text: I want more Originium fuel for a warmer winter.

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: ...I want more police stations, and I wanna become a cop. I want to give, not take.

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Depressed Soldier
steps.text: I... I hope Mum's still waiting for me back home.

steps.name: Cheerful Soldier
steps.text: Hah, don't worry! She'll be there to open the door for you.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: What about you, Dagda? You gonna stick with us to get the gym back in business, or will you lock yourself away in your tower?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: You and I, we've got a score to settle, Hannah.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Let's go back to the gym together, Vina!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Yes, we will... we haven't found Baird yet...

a.text: One more step until we're home. That one step took us three days.

spans.text: One more step until we're home. That one step took us three days.

a.text: We were welcomed by steam gushing from the factories, reaching into the clouds.

spans.text: We were welcomed by steam gushing from the factories, reaching into the clouds.

a.text: But many didn't live to see it. They walked into the tunnel, singing, and never came out again.

spans.text: But many didn't live to see it. They walked into the tunnel, singing, and never came out again.

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: Have one on me, Vina!

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: The devils ran, but they're not dead yet! They still have that tech that filled the city with Originium dust. They'll be back, mark my words!

steps.name: Impetuous Soldier
steps.text: And you can bet those dukes won't give a shit about us when something happens again.

steps.name: Impetuous Soldier
steps.text: Like you said, we need to defend ourselves.

steps.name: Impetuous Soldier
steps.text: That's why I don't believe the rumors that say the Exemplars are getting disbanded. Right, Vina?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Do you remember the wishes we made at the access port?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: For the factory boilers to burn bright as they used to, for the guns on Londinium's walls to defend her as they used to.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: For the doors of the police stations to be wide open to all, for the police to defy the nobles' will and treat the Infected with fairness and justice.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: For the law of Parliament to be the only rule... that's what I hope to see, and what I'm trying to bring about.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Are you happy with Londinium now? Has she gotten better?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I can tell you that I'm not happy.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: You're dodging the question, Madam Speaker.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: If you choose to do nothing and keep the status quo of the Exemplars, that's entirely fine with everyone.

steps.name: Shearer
steps.text: All they want is an answer. Will the Exemplars continue to exist—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: This is my answer, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: What Parliament fears is your trust in me, personally, that runs deeper than your trust in Parliament itself.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Perhaps they fear that the Exemplars will become the private army of Vina Victoria.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: What will become of the glory and honor of the Exemplars when that day comes?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Will the day come when our wishes come true?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Thank you. I will inform Parliament of what I learned today. It's not my place to give an answer over the heads of Parliament.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Let's go, Morgan.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Morgan?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: You go first, Vina. I'll have a couple of rounds with the guys here.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: ...Sure.

a.text: I didn't understand what Vina said that day.

spans.text: I didn't understand what Vina said that day.

a.text: But I agreed with the Lieutenant. Our Exemplar comrades needed our help. That's why I needed to stay, stay on Vina's behalf, at least talk to them.

spans.text: But I agreed with the Lieutenant. Our Exemplar comrades needed our help. That's why I needed to stay, stay on Vina's behalf, at least talk to them.

a.text: Even though she was the Speaker, and there was so much she could do...

spans.text: Even though she was the Speaker, and there was so much she could do...

a.text: For the first time since the war ended, I drank until I passed out. It burned my belly.

spans.text: For the first time since the war ended, I drank until I passed out. It burned my belly.

a.text: It was Hannah who found me, and I asked her the question that I could never ask Vina—

spans.text: It was Hannah who found me, and I asked her the question that I could never ask Vina—

a.text: When can we go home, back to our gym?

spans.text: When can we go home, back to our gym?

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: The herbs are growing well. Diane would be glad.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: When the farm was rebuilt, it was she who persuaded the engineers to leave behind the damaged lighting equipment and refit it for small greenhouses that didn't draw so much power.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Sorry... remind me, where were we?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: We were talking about your condition.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: You mentioned that you noticed a significant increase in the strength of your Originium Arts.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Yes. Sorry, I'm finding it hard to remember things lately. Keep getting distracted. The doctor says Originium has made its way into my brain...

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Don't tell me, I've told you this before too?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: We're just chatting. You can say anything you want. Anything else that doesn't feel right?

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Difficulty walking straight? It's happening to a lot of people, though.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Ataxia. It's a common symptom of many Infected in Londinium, but I'm not sure what the cause is.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: When I'm by myself, I've been trying to... it's strange. My Originium Arts seem to be changing.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Changing? I don't have any other reports of—

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Never mind. Please continue, Sarah.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Are you casting with your bare hands, by the way? The doctors may have told you this already, but that's detrimental to keeping your condition under control.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Heh. You're a worrier alright, just like Diane said.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: I just can't help it. It's how I search for the war memories in my clouded mind.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: The battle for the walls.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: You said you were a nurse, and you were trying to stop a witchcraft bomb explosion with your Arts, but it didn't work out too well.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Yes. I remember I was behind Lieutenant Shearer, and the blast threw me off my feet.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: Next thing I remember, I was in the field hospital, lying next to the other acute Infected.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: I don't know how many witchcraft bombs fell upon the Exemplars.

steps.name: Sanatorium Patient
steps.text: So many fates, turned on their heads in an instant... but I didn't see any of it, and I don't remember any of it... how could things be like this?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Sarah?
The patient is trembling, and begins to cast Originium Arts without realizing it.
Eliseo does not know if it is a symptom of post-traumatic stress, but he quickly attempts to direct her attention elsewhere.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Listen to me, Sarah. Take a deep breath.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Can you smell the flowers? You're in the sanatorium.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: The war is over. The Exemplars are home. You're back in Londinium.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: You're...
He pauses and looks up at the damaged lighting above his head.
A strange and unfamiliar city, one that, to his eyes, is not far off from a pile of rubble.
'You're in... a place where everything will get better.'

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: The alteration of Sarah's Originium Arts is a symptom that has never been observed in other Infected. I should ask my colleagues to keep an eye out.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: I wonder if Diane could get me in touch with an international Messenger. Waiting for Maylander's regular Messenger would take too long. Londinium needs supplies, urgently...

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Eliseo! You're here too?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: —Why didn't you stop her? Weren't you looking for her?

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Who?

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: The Speaker.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: The Speaker?! I saw her coming out of an underground pub...

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: That's where I came from. I happened to run into her when she went to have a drink with old friends.

steps.name: Eliseo
steps.text: Sounds like she really considers herself your friend.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Yeah... if only she considered herself more than a friend.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Eliseo... I've always felt that Londinium could become a better place, that Victoria would be proud of her.

steps.name: Diane
steps.text: Can the Speaker really make that happen, though?
